context.objective: Document how we carry out Investment Purchases: Recording, Setup & Controls, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Let me start from the back end because that is what I think of first. The very last thing I do as the investment accounting preparer is reconcile the Investment Payable clearing account 20080 for that purchase: the cash entry debits 20080 and the cost entry credits 20080, so for the finished event it has to net to zero, or any leftover has to be a supported timing item with an owner and an age. In that same last step I confirm the Allvue setup and CRM attributes are complete, that cost, shares and ownership evidence agree across records, and then the second reviewer and I sign off the checklists and we keep the deal bible. That is the end. Going right back to the beginning, what starts it is the client telling us about a completed or imminent investment purchase. That notice is the trigger, and the first thing I do after it is open the New Investment Set Up checklist and the purchase control checklist. Separately, the 20080 account also gets checked and cleared every quarter.
What do you do next after opening the New Investment Set Up and purchase control checklists?

Still in that opening step, I record the fund or entity, the issuer or portfolio company, security type, purchase or closing date, cost or funding amount, counterparty and payment date. I assign the preparer, second reviewer, the callback or Treasury person, the compliance screening person and the approval roles, and I classify the deal: equity, debt, SAFE or note conversion, non-cash restructuring, fund of funds or another supported category. If the structure or ownership is unclear I escalate before going on. Now I will jump ahead a bit: the Investment Attribute Form comes two steps after the opening. On it I record the investment name and portfolio company name exactly as approved, closing date, industry, security type, shares or units, cost lines, the FAS 157 level and the client signer, I compare every attribute to the supporting document or written client direction, and the client provides or approves anything missing; the second reviewer checks it. Missing or conflicting attributes must be resolved before any system setup. But before that form, sitting between the opening step and the form, is collecting and validating the deal document package, which we call the deal bible: purchase agreement, cap table, structure chart, ownership evidence and closing documents. I confirm the approved investment, legal entities, security, shares, cost, closing date, payment terms and restrictions, log anything missing or still in draft in a deficiency log and get it before the step that depends on it. The reviewer checks completeness. Legal interpretation questions go to the client or legal counsel, we do not infer terms.
Once the Investment Attribute Form is complete and its attributes are resolved, what happens next?

Let me give you the Allvue part first because it is the most hands-on, then what sits just before it. In Allvue NAV I create or validate the Issuer, then the Security with the approved type and attributes, then the Lot using the approved closing, share and cost information, then I create or apply the approved Allocation rule, strictly in that order. Then in Allvue CRM I update Firm Known As, Industry and FAS 157 level, and I compare the system fields back to the Attribute Form. The second reviewer checks the setup. A duplicate master, wrong entity or security type, missing field or unsupported allocation gets escalated to the system owner and the reviewer. But that Allvue setup is not directly after the form. Between the form and Allvue is the approval and counterparty clearance step: we retain the client or GP approval of the purchase, amount, counterparty and payment; Treasury validates new counterparty bank details by callback; the compliance screening role runs Exiger screening if the jurisdiction meets the approved high-risk criteria; any bank or screening discrepancy is resolved; and we confirm the payment date and that the bank cut-off is feasible. Payment is held for a failed callback, a high-risk alert, missing approval or a missed cut-off. Then after Allvue, Treasury releases the payment, and once the money has gone I prepare the cash entry.
Which role is accountable for the overall investment-purchase result?

I do not know. The overall process owner and the final accountable approver have not been confirmed, and neither have the exact titles of the preparer and the second reviewer. What I can say is who does what: I prepare, the second reviewer checks, the client or GP approves the investment, Treasury releases payment, and the entries go to approval groups. And I need to fix something I told you a moment ago. Actually I had that backwards: the cash entry comes before the payment, not after. The true order after the Allvue setup is: first I prepare the cash entry in the Daily Posting process, debit Investment Payable 20080 and credit the correct bank account, with a description that is different from the later cost entry, attach the client approval, callback and screening evidence, deal and payment support and the calculation, and route it to all AFCs, FCs and Directors, resolve their comments and get the approvals. Only after that approved cash entry does Treasury submit the payment through the treasury workflow and release it sufficiently before the bank cut-off. Then we record payment status, the bank settlement date, the bank reference and any rejection or return, and compare the actual cash disbursed to the approved cash entry. A rejected or returned payment, changed instructions, a cut-off miss or an amount mismatch gets escalated. I do not know what AFC and FC stand for or in what order those approvers sign, that has not been defined.
What happens to the purchase or its stakeholders if a recording or control failure is not caught?

Several things. Cash could leave without client or GP approval, verified bank details or screening, which is exactly why payment is never released until approval, callback, required screening, the internal entry approval and cut-off feasibility are all done. The investment could be recorded with the wrong cost, shares or attributes, or as a duplicate or misconfigured security, and that flows into allocation, reporting and the later debt investment processing. If the cash and cost entries carry identical descriptions, activity can be suppressed in reporting and the reconciliation breaks. And a non-zero 20080 balance keeps the item open and prevents closeout; we identify the missing or mismatched entry or the timing item, assign an owner, age and escalate it, and we never force an entry just to clear the account. That reminds me there is a piece I have not told you yet, and it sits after the payment and before the final reconciliation I started with: the cost entry. Once payment is confirmed and we have final deal documents and approved cost support, I confirm the final acquisition cost, prepare the General Operations entry debiting Investment Acquisition 11010 and crediting Investment Payable 20080, with a description different from the cash entry, attach final documents, the Attribute Form, setup evidence and cost support, and route it to FCs and Directors; it is posted after their approval. If final documents are not available yet, we do not make the cost entry: only the supported cash entry stands, 20080 stays open as a timing item with an owner and aging, and setup cannot close until the documents arrive.
How do you determine the final acquisition cost from the deal documents and cost support?

It comes from the final executed purchase or conversion documents and the approved allocation, never from a provisional Attribute Form or an old client workbook. I confirm the cash and any supported non-cash components, and principal and accrued interest where that applies, and the cost entry has to agree to those final documents. Where part of a combined purchase cost is allocated to a warrant or option, I only reclassify the client-approved amount and prove that base investment cost plus warrant or option cost equals the total cost before allocation. Beyond that I do not have a set formula or entry template to give you, those are not specified. Two conditional pieces I skipped, and both sit after the cost entry and before the final 20080 reconciliation and sign-off. First, only where a SAFE, convertible note or non-cash conversion applies: for a SAFE I apply the executed cap or discount terms, for a note I include principal and accrued interest only as the executed terms require, I work out the resulting security and shares and update the Allvue issuer, security and lot records, use Investment Restructure In 11021 and the approved Restructure Out account, and reconcile the old instrument coming off against the new one with no unexplained value; the reviewer checks it. I do not know which Restructure Out account, that is not confirmed, so we get approved accounting direction. Second, after that, only where applicable: escrow and fund of funds. I identify any escrow receivable and get the client tax department direction before recording escrow treatment, and for a fund of funds I calculate concentration against partners capital; if the supported calculation is over 5 percent the disclosure is routed to the financial reporting process. If neither applies I document that it is not applicable and go straight to the final reconciliation.
How does the client’s purchase notice typically reach you?
This capture still has open sections. 12 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.
